_doc2: rendererString replaces only the UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL text the app reads to pick its class (a laptop with an Intel UHD 620, a Snapdragon phone with an Adreno 740, a budget phone with a Mali-G52); the GPU behind it is still this machine's. The numbers measured before the performance round ran the old code, which never read that string.
_doc: Synthetic device classes for scripts/perf-bench.mjs. Everything runs on one Apple M1 Max, so a profile can only slow the machine down: CPU throttling (CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate) is real main-thread slowdown; network throttling (CDP Network.emulateNetworkConditions) is real transfer shaping; the GPU is the real Apple GPU unless gpu is 'swiftshader' (pure software rasteriser, a hard lower bound) or gpuLoad adds competing GPU work from OffscreenCanvas workers (a rough proxy for a GPU 1/(workers+1) as fast, not a real iGPU). deviceMemory and hardwareConcurrency are overridden by an init script, they do not limit the machine.

desktop-gpu.label: Desktop with a discrete or Apple-silicon GPU

laptop-igpu.label: Thin laptop with an integrated GPU (about 3x slower GPU, 2x slower CPU)
laptop-igpu.rendererString: ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620 Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)
emulated: gpu (competing OffscreenCanvas load on the same GPU)

phone-high.label: Recent flagship phone, Slow 4G
emulated: gpu (not throttled: the Apple GPU is far faster than a phone GPU)

potato.label: Software rendering (SwiftShader), 1280x720, CPU 4x
emulated: cpu (throttle on the main thread only: SwiftShader rasterises in the GPU process, which the throttle does not touch)
